slides.headline: Slide 1
slides.body: What happens when there's nothing to find

slides.headline: Slide 2
slides.body: A homeowner needs a plumber, electrician, or handyman today, not next week.

slides.headline: Slide 3
slides.body: They search. Three names come up. If you're not one of them, this job was never yours to lose — it just never reached you.

slides.headline: Slide 4
slides.body: You never see the search. You never know the job existed. There's no missed call to notice, no lead to follow up on.

slides.headline: Slide 5
slides.body: The work you're best at doesn't matter if it never gets seen. That's the whole problem a website solves.

slides.headline: Slide 6
slides.body: We build the site that shows up. — Trevo

caption1.variantA:
We reviewed a contractor site that had everything except a way to call.

Nice logo. Clean colors. A whole page about the company history. Somewhere near the bottom, in small text, a contact form.

No phone number anywhere above it. No tap-to-call. Just a form, on a site that's mostly viewed on a phone, by someone standing in a driveway wanting to talk to a person.

This is a composite of a pattern we see constantly, not one specific business. The fix isn't a redesign. It's one button, moved to the top.

Link in bio to see what yours could look like.

— Trevo

trevo_found.body:
Here's what's inside a Trevo handyman site.

A service menu with real photos, not stock images.
Tap-to-call above the fold, one thumb reach.
A quick quote request form for jobs that don't need a phone call to start.
Google reviews pulled in automatically.
Trust badges shown clearly, right where a homeowner is deciding whether to trust you.

That's the build. — Trevo
